messages:
incidents-bot: ALERT: spike in container restarts on prod-pool-7 (host=prod-gpu-07). Reason: CUDA OOM during prefill phase. Auto-shed engaged and rate limiter tripped.

alice_oncall: I'm on it. Root message ts 1791012345. Any immediate customer errors?

incidents-bot: 503/502 surge observed for endpoints chat/long-context. 18 errors in last 5m; latency also up.

ben_infra: quick dump: host prod-gpu-07 shows multiple container restarts. dmesg: `NVRM: Xid (79): GPU has fallen off the bus` plus runtime log lines indicating failed KV allocations.

carla_sre: can we match requests with large context header and route them to degraded-quality path? We have an older small-model fleet (fallback-small) that tolerates long contexts by truncating.

alice_oncall: plan in 3 bullets: 1) add temporary edge rule to route requests with header `X-Context-Tokens` > 55000 to fallback-small; 2) cordon + drain prod-gpu-07; 3) hotpatch runtime to early-fail if requested KV alloc > 11GB (return 413 instead of crash).

flo_research: FYI some customers intentionally send ~80k token histories. Trimming will change outputs substantially. Recommend telling support to expect escalations.

dan_support: will prepare a short customer advisory. Draft: "We've detected OOMs for extremely long context requests. Traffic with very large context is temporarily routed to a smaller compatible model to keep service available. You may observe reduced quality for very long prompts."

eva_prod: add CSMs for the 4 affected enterprise orgs, please. Also post in #customer-updates.

ben_infra: cordon prod-gpu-07: `kubectl cordon prod-gpu-07` -> done. Draining pods now with `kubectl drain prod-gpu-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30`

ben_infra: observed runtime snippet from crash:
```
2026-06-04T09:12:11Z runtime[4567]: prefill tokens=80432, kv_alloc=14.7GB
runtime: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
runtime: terminating container, restart requested
NVRM: Xid (79): GPU has fallen off the bus
```

carla_sre: applying nginx lua rule to inspect `X-Context-Tokens` and rewrite backend to `/v1/generate?model=fallback-small`. Pushing rule now.

alice_oncall: rule applied. Watching traffic.

flo_research: telemetry: prefill-oom rate on prod-gpu-07 falling immediately, but small rise on other hosts as they take rerouted load.

carla_sre: deploying runtime hotpatch to canary (20%): cap per-request KV to 11GB and return 413 with body `{\"error\":\"context too large: reduce tokens\"}` when exceeded. This prevents kernel oom.

alice_oncall: canary behavior ok: canary nodes early-fail and do not restart. Proceed to roll to 100% unless objections.

ben_infra: drain finished on prod-gpu-07; scheduling hardware reboot + driver revalidation. Filing ticket INFRA-8012.

dan_support: posted customer advisory at 09:25 UTC and notified CSMs. Monitoring inbound support threads.

eva_prod: action items assigned: ben_infra -> reproduce in staging and collect driver stack; carla_sre -> backfill hotpatch to production and add metrics for early-413; flo_research -> propose graceful fallback policy that steps model quality down progressively rather than a single jump; dan_support -> keep customer comms updated.

alice_oncall: keeping pager open for another 60m to watch for reflares. Current status: restarts dropped to baseline, error rate reduced to ~3/min.

maya_ops: :thumbsup: Nice work. Suggest we add a post-incident note to the runbook for matching `X-Context-Tokens` header at the edge.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT mitigated: host prod-gpu-07 drained, routing rule applied, hotpatch rolled. See INFRA-8012 and runbook PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runbooks/prefill-fanout-throttle.

alice_oncall: closing pager; moving follow-ups to #postmortem-prefill-oom. Thanks team.
